reasons.observation: Both descriptions name the Fender Player II Stratocaster with an alder body, maple neck, SSS pickups and a 2-point synchronized tremolo, so they appear to be the same model family.
The IDs differ (d4PJDa4 for the shop, 0yRC8r4 for the competitor). Channel3 treats these as separate catalog entries, which often means different variants.
The URL slug says 'black-with-maple-fingerboard' (StratP2MBK). The competitor's own description and structured_attributes say the fingerboard is rosewood, so its data conflicts with itself.

The shop listing has variants null, and its title and description give no colour. Its structured attributes list a rosewood fingerboard, so the colour and fingerboard of the shop's variant cannot be confirmed against the competitor's black/maple-slug item.
The title is generic ('Stratocaster Electric Guitar') and omits 'Player II' and any colour, so it does not identify the exact model on its own.
Condition is null, so it cannot be confirmed as new rather than used, refurbished or open-box.

The listed price of 99 USD is far below the shop's 849.99 USD for the same model family. This may point to a data error or a non-guitar item, but I am not judging price. It lowers my confidence in the listing data.
Both listings have variants null, so no selected size, colour or finish can be compared directly. The fingerboard conflict in the competitor's data remains unresolved.
